stemMd:
A study compares two ways of cataloguing a collection. One method records many short descriptions quickly; the other produces fewer entries but includes detailed information about provenance. Researchers find that the better method depends on whether users need broad discovery or precise historical interpretation.

Which choice best states the main idea?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Detailed entries are always inferior to brief ones.

options.label: B
options.textMd: All users ask identical questions about collections.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Catalogues are useful only when every object has a long description.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The value of a cataloguing method depends on the purpose for which the catalogue will be used.

explanationMd: The text compares methods without declaring one universally superior. It explicitly ties their relative value to discovery versus historical interpretation.

distractorRationale.a: The text gives each method a useful role.
distractorRationale.b: Different user needs drive the conclusion.
distractorRationale.c: Broad discovery can benefit from numerous short entries.
